episodes.205124: An upper level weather system moved across the Southern Plains on August 29th. As this occurred, showers and thunderstorms developed off the high terrain of New Mexico and southeast Colorado. They moved to the south and east into the Texas and Oklahoma Panhandles during the late afternoon into the evening hours. These storms became severe and brought hail and damaging wind gusts to the region. In addition, ample atmospheric moisture was in place, which led to heavy rainfall.
episodes.205125: An upper level weather system moved across the Southern Plains on August 29th. As this occurred, showers and thunderstorms developed off the high terrain of New Mexico and southeast Colorado. They moved to the south and east into the Texas and Oklahoma Panhandles during the late afternoon into the evening hours. These storms became severe and brought hail and damaging wind gusts to the region. In addition, ample atmospheric moisture was in place, which led to heavy rainfall.
episodes.205153: Monsoon Moisture across central and eastern New Mexico along with a backdoor front entering northeast NM resulted in the development of scattered shower and thunderstorm activity across these portions of the state. A slow moving thunderstorm resulted in flash flooding on State Highway 76 near Chimayo. Severe thunderstorms resulted in damaging wind gusts of up to 70 mph across Union and Harding County. Finally, mid to late evening thunderstorms resulted in some flash flooding at Bear Canyon near Ruidoso and in Portales.
episodes.205352: Marine showers produced a waterspout near Galveston.
episodes.205439: A stationary boundary draped across Southeast New Mexico and West Texas became a focus for shower and thunderstorm development during the afternoon of the 29th. A few storms produced damaging wind gusts, and some urban flooding was reported in Odessa.
episodes.205440: A stationary boundary draped across Southeast New Mexico and West Texas became a focus for shower and thunderstorm development during the afternoon of the 29th. A few storms produced damaging wind gusts, and some urban flooding was reported in Odessa.
episodes.205443: Similar to August 29th, a dissipating stationary boundary served as a focus for shower and thunderstorm development. Upslope flow also contributed to additional thunderstorm development in the higher terrain of West Texas. One storm managed to produce a severe wind gust near Marathon.
episodes.206162: In the afternoon of the 29th, a few isolated storms formed across northwestern Kansas and proceeded to the southeast. These storms produced 60 MPH winds that caused damage, as well as 1.5 inch hail.
episodes.206336: A stalled front lingering over the area combined with daytime heating, high moisture and a passing short-wave trough aloft produced localized heavy rainfall.
episodes.206338: A lingering front, high moisture and daytime instability under a passing short-wave trough aloft produced locally heavy rainfall.
episodes.206609: Thunderstorms developed along a stationary frontal boundary, situated over the western Sandhills, during the mid afternoon hours of August 29th. This activity grew upscale into the late afternoon and early evening hours as it traveled east and south, producing hail up to half dollar size in Lincoln County.
episodes.206661: A weak frontal boundary stalled along Interstate 10 during late August. The boundary helped spark numerous showers and storms with one producing flooding in Sulphur.
episodes.206739: An upper high over the Permian Basin brought deep monsoonal moisture into far west Texas.  Early evening thunderstorms developed over the Fabens area and brought over 2 inches of rain and flash flooding to the area.
episodes.206807: A slow-moving summer frontal system, in conjunction with occasional disturbances embedded within the northwest flow aloft, generated multiple rounds of thunderstorms both preceding and during the Labor Day weekend. The predominant hazard observed was flash flooding, attributed to the substantial rainfall produced by some of these storms.
episodes.206924: A trough of low pressure over the eastern United States, a stationary surface boundary north of the area, and ample moisture over South Florida created an environment where strong thunderstorms developed over Atlantic waters off Southeast Florida on August 30, 2025.
episodes.206983: Isolated showers and a few weak thunderstorms developed in cyclonic flow to the north of a low pressure system centered over central South Dakota. A short lived landspout tornado developed south of Zap in Mercer County. The tornado touched down in an open field and impacted no structures. There was no damage to evaluate. By National Weather Service policy the tornado is rated EF-U (Unknown).
episodes.207103: Scattered strong to severe storms develop across the plains throughout the day, with one producing measured severe gusts during the evening hours.
episodes.207149: A tropical wave moving south of the islands, moisture, local effects, excessive diurnal heating, and sea breeze variations, promoted the formation of showers and thunderstorms over the islands during the last two days of the month. Flooding was reported in Yauco and Carolina, while a fatal lightning strike was reported in Toa Vaca Lake, Villalba.
episodes.207211: A lower tropospheric trough had moved southward over the Florida Peninsula, producing a broad zone of confluent, moist flow across the Florida Keys.  Several waterspouts were observed south of Marathon, Florida.
episodes.207670: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms dropped southeast from the Nebraska Sandhills and into south central Nebraska during evening hours. Initially, a fairly isolated thunderstorm moved into Valley county, prompted a Severe Thunderstorm Warning and produced a 65 mph wind gust. As that storm moved into Sherman county, tree damage was reported near Loup City by the Emergency Manager. Eventually, more storms developed to the west, again oozing south/southeast with time. The Kearney Airport reported a 61 mph wind gust and a 62 mph wind gusts occurred southwest of Minden. Though the thunderstorms did produce 60 mph wind gusts in spots, the storms were largely sub-severe and that kept wind damage to a minimum. ||As can be typical for late August, thunderstorms developed to the northwest and spread southeast in a northwest atmospheric flow. The thunderstorms developed as a subtle shortwave slid southeast in the flow. As the storms moved southeast, they encountered slightly better effective shear of 30-45 knots. However, the missing link was the instability. The area was in the midst of a late summer cool-down with lower dewpoints than normal and a drier and less unstable air mass overall. Mid-level lapse rates were also only marginally unstable. While there were a few severe wind reports, the limited instability and weaker flow in late August gave the thunderstorms more ���bark than bite��� despite their pretty impressive radar appearance.

events.narrative: A report was received from the public via mPING of street/road flooding 2 miles SW of Mission Dorado. The total time of occurrence is partially estimated by radar. No damage was reported.
A chicken coop was blown away in Brewster, KS.

An NWS employee reported a stalled vehicle in 1-2 feet of water over the road at Highway 385 (Andrews Highway) and 52nd Street in Odessa. The total time of occurrence is partially estimated by radar. The cost of damages is also estimated.

A broken power pole was reported at Highway 385 (Andrews Highway) and 93rd Street in Odessa. The time of occurrence is estimated by radar. The maximum wind gust is estimated, as well as the cost of damages.
Report of a semi truck blown over on I-70 at mile marker 7.
Wind gusts were estimated to be near 65 MPH.
The Mesonet station FW0979 Hobbs measured a 69 mph wind gust. The time of occurrence is partially estimated.
Wind gusts estimated to be near 60 MPH resulted in a few small limbs downed onto Highway 58 just northwest of Loup City.
The West Texas Mesonet station 5 NW Hobbs NM measured a 69 mph wind gust.
Runoff from heavy rainfall on the Salt burn scar resulted in about 1 foot of rushing water flooding grassland at the base of Bear Canyon, according to video from the Ruidoso emergency manager.
The first severe wind gust occurred at 2007CDT. The peak gust of 61mph occurred at 2012 CDT at the mesonet site located 12 miles southwest of Dalhart.
Radar estimated almost 2.5 inches of rainfall north of Fabens which created ponding of water as well as water running into structures including a restaurant in the area.
ASOS station KLAA Lamar Airport measured a 66 mph wind gust.
A private weather station in Palm Coast measured 2.35 inches between 10 pm and 11:45 pm.
A wind gust of 61 MPH was measured by the Kearney Airport AWOS.
A wind gust of 62 MPH was measured by a mesonet located four miles west-southwest of Minden.
A wind gust of 73 MPH was measured by a mesonet station located three miles north-northeast of Hildreth.
Heavy rainfall from thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding on numerous streets in Portales. This included 18th Street which was flooded with 6 to 8 inches of water over the road.

Heavy rain in Sulphur caused Bayou d'Inde to rise out of its banks. Street flooding affected a portion of the city as well after 5.67 fell in just over an hour. Three inches of water also flooded the gymnasium at Sulphur High School.
US-75 northbound was closed due to flooding in a construction zone.
A broadcast media video indicated flooding on northbound I-35E near Market Center Blvd in Dallas.
A public report indicated that the westbound Interstate 30 frontage road was covered with one foot of water near the Erby Campbell exit.
The city of Dallas FRWS gauges indicated that Luna Road at Y Street, and Tantor Road at X Street in northwest Dallas were flooded and closed.

events.county: High Is To Freeport Tx Out 20Nm
events.narrative: Numerous photos and videos were shared on social media, showing a waterspout near Galveston island, around 45th street beach. Broadcast media reported that the waterspout moved on to the beach, blowing over umbrellas and chairs. However, no injuries were reported.
Mesonet station XKBS Biscayne Bay Light 20 reported a wind gust of 39 mph at 2:08pm as a gusty thunderstorm moved over Biscayne Bay.

events.county: Deerfield Beach To Ocean Reef Fl
events.narrative: Social media video of a waterspout with a visible spray ring just east of Porgy Key from footage taken by a boater in Biscayne Bay.
A social media report indicated that Main Street at the railroad trestle, and Castle Dr between Dexham Rd and Rowlett Rd, were flooded and closed in the city of Rowlett.
A City of Dallas Flooded Roadway Warning System gauge indicated that the 7400 block of Merriman Pkwy was flooded and closed along White Rock Creek in Dallas.
The tornado touched down in an open field south of Zap and impacted no structures. There was no damage to evaluate. By National Weather Service policy the tornado is rated EF-U (Unknown).

The 911 Call Center reported that at approximately 3:20 PM AST, a lightning strike impacted two individuals in a boat near the fishing club by the dam at Lago Toa Vaca. One individual was reported conscious with burns to the hands but breathing. The second individual, a 48 year old male, was thrown into the water by the impact; his body was found at around 8 PM ast.
A mesonet station TT687 Indian Lake Sf measured 2.97 inches of rain. Rain began  around 410 PM.
The West Texas Mesonet station 166 Marathon 21N measured two 58 mph wind gusts.

events.county: Straits Of Florida From Craig Key To West End Of Seven Mile Bridge Out 20 Nm
events.narrative: Up to four waterspouts were observed south of Marathon in the Straits of Florida and reported via social media.  The first waterspout was observed in shared video to be very narrow, mature, with a visible spray ring, and tilted at a 45-degree angle.  A second waterspout observed by shared video appeared to be less mature with the condensation funnel reaching approximately halfway down from cloud base, and with a very faint spray ring.  This waterspout had very minimal tilt.  The parent convective cells were moving toward the east at 10 to 15 knots.
